correctness.summary: For any two equal-length windows, including overlapping windows, exact equality has probability d^{-k}. Above the logarithmic length threshold, the deficit from position-limited maximum is dominated by the number of colliding window pairs, yielding a geometric all-moment sum; below the threshold a deterministic alphabet-size bound suffices. For centered concentration, the longest-repeated-substring tail gives a high-probability set on which total complexity is Hamming-Lipschitz, after which McShane extension, Efron--Stein and McDiarmid yield the stated variance and tail bounds. Exact finite checks confirm the combinatorial identities used in the proof on small cases.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Janson--Lonardi--Szpankowski already give precise first-moment asymptotics for total sequence complexity, Flaxman--Harrow--Sorkin treat the deterministic maximum, Ahmadi--Ward study second moments for fixed-length subword complexity, and Gaither--Ward study suffix-tree internal-profile variance. Searches using total subword complexity, factor complexity, distinct-substring count, suffix-array longest-common-prefix sums, and longest repeated substrings did not locate the all-q deficit estimate or a variance/concentration theorem for the total all-length statistic. Older analytic suffix-tree literature under an equivalent additive-functional formulation is the main residual risk.

value.summary: The result directly supplies variance and concentration information for a recently highlighted gap while also showing exponential control of the deficit from exact maximum. The proofs are elementary enough to be reusable and clearly separate total all-length complexity from previously studied fixed-length or fixed-level statistics.

limitations: The results assume independent uniform letters and fixed alphabet size.
The O_d(n log^4 n) variance upper bound is not claimed to be sharp.
No matching lower bound, asymptotic variance, central limit theorem, or optimal concentration scale is proved.
The constants in the deficit tail were not optimized.
Fixed-length second moments, deterministic maxima, and suffix-tree internal-profile variance are prior work.
Older analytic suffix-tree or longest-common-prefix literature may contain an equivalent total-functional formulation that was not located.
Independent audit has not been performed.
